arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Mr. Stewart argued the records involve the government's trustee duties.
Mr. Hitchings argued Exemption 5 excludes communications with non-agency parties.
The association claims these communications allocate valuable rights among outsiders.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Department of Interior seeks to keep seven documents private. These records relate to the government's role as trustee for Indian tribes. The Klamath Water Users Protective Association wants the public to see these files. The case tests the scope of a specific FOIA exemption.

paragraphs: The Supreme Court heard oral argument in this case on January 10, 2001.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: The Department of Interior wants the Court to uphold the lower court's denial of the documents.
The Klamath Water Users Protective Association wants the Court to order the release of the seven documents.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: The government argues Exemption 5 covers these trustee-related records.
The association argues Exemption 5 does not cover communications with outside parties.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the boundary of government transparency. It determines when agencies can hide records shared with outside groups. The outcome shapes public access to federal resource management decisions.
